data.text:
Imaran Khan vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 4 January, 2024 
Author: Ashwani Kumar Mishra
Bench: Ashwani Kumar Mishra
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:1525-Db
Court No. - 32
Case :- Writ - C No. - 43859 of 2023
Petitioner :- Imaran Khan
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 4 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Chandra Prakash Garg 
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Ashwani Kumar Mishra,J.
Hon'ble Syed Qamar Hasan Rizvi,J.
Heard learned counsel for the parties. 
The petitioner appears to be running a shop in which he sells meat etc. According to the petitioner,
he has obtained requisite permission from the competent authority under the Food Safety Act,
2006.. He has approached this Court challenging a notice issued by the Executive Officer, Nagar Panchayat, Baberu, Banda dated 16.10.2023, which records that the activities undertaken by the petitioner are in contravention of the bye-laws framed by the Nagar Panchayat, as are notified in the Gazette on 17.07.2021. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that though a reply to it has been submitted but no decision is being taken in the matter and he is being compelled to close down his Imaran Khan vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 4 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197523488/
1 shop. 
Learned Standing Counsel states that the competent authority shall take an appropriate decision in the matter. 
Considering the nature of order proposed to be passed, we do not deem it necessary to issue notice to 5th respondent. 
Since the petitioner has already submitted his reply to the notice, we deem it appropriate to direct the respondents to accord consideration to the petitioner's reply to the notice dated 16.10.2023 and 14.11.2023 by passing a reasoned order within a period of four weeks from the date of presentation of a certified copy of this order. The writ petition is disposed off, accordingly. 
Order Date :- 4.1.2024 Pkb/
